chapter: Kirby again, Garland gigs and later recordings
title: Retelling how he joined Kirby in Washington
summary: Kirby offered a two-week Washington job; there was no rehearsal and the book was torn, and 'Sunny Side of the Street' won him a raise.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Quitting the band: why sidemen left

blocks.x: Then we've already done the part where you went off on the USO tour...
And then shortly after you got back, you went with Kirby. And we discussed that earlier too, but I'd like to repeat how you first got with him and you were told to go to Washington.

Yeah. He came by my house, and asked me was I doing anything the week coming up. I told him, "No, I'm not doin' anything no time." I had nothing booked up, absolutely nothing. So he says, "Well, I've got a couple of weeks in Washington, if you care to go down there with me, in a nightclub." So I told him, "All right, make the engagement. How much do it pay?" And he told me. I told him, "Okay, that's all right." He told me to meet him at the Brown Derby Club on the following Monday, where they were opening up. So he asked me did I have enough to get to Washington, and I said, "Yeah, I have enough to get there." "You don't want to draw no money?" I said, "No."
He told to me to meet him in this hotel, and I met him there the following Monday. I got in his hotel, and all the band was there. And I thought we were going to rehearse,

since I was the new man in the band. They were just around there, talking, just passing the time away. They said, "Well, let's go." I thought we was gonna rehearse somewhere. They said, "No, we're going to the club." They open up at eight o'clock. "Well, what about the rehearsal?" He said, "No, we don't have time to rehearse. We rehearse on the job."

So anyway, we get to the job, and he opens up this music book, and it looks like somebody had been... Well, the book was in bad condition, very bad condition, and the music was torn and dirty, you couldn't see it. The lights in the club were very dark, and you couldn't see it anyway. They didn't have any music stands, so you had to put the music on the floor.

So anyway, we played a couple of numbers. Well, it went over all right. So then he said, "Well, let's play 'Sunny Side Of The Street.'" So we started off "Sunny Side." So after the trumpet played the first chorus, he told me to take a chorus. And after one, he started shouting, and one-thing-and-another, he was so glad. "Take another chorus, Charlie!" So I take another chorus. Oh, he was so thrilled. And I got through playing, people are applauding -- he was tickled to death.
So when we come off the bandstand, he came and threw

his arm around my shoulders: "What did I promise to pay you?" So I told him. He says, "Well, now you got a raise." I said, "Well, that's fine." I didn't ask him what the raise was because I didn't want to appear to be greedy. But I knew he would be all right, because he was a pretty generous guy anyway. So he says, "Come on, let's have a drink."
